  "text": "Martin arrived with six cardboard boxes, though Ruth had told him three would do.

“They were free,” he said.

“That doesn’t mean we have to fill them.”

He set them on the kitchen table. One had held bananas. There were air holes in the sides.

The freezer was already empty. Ruth had taken the last bag of runner beans home on Sunday and cooked them until they lost their colour.

“Council’s collecting the bed tomorrow,” she said.

“What time?”

“They wouldn’t say.”

Martin opened the cupboard beside the cooker. Plates stood in their rack, largest at the back. He took down a yellow mug.

“You want this?”

“The handle gets hot.”

“I remember.”

He wrapped it in newspaper anyway.

Ruth pulled a chair towards the sink and climbed onto it. Above the cupboards she found a biscuit tin, an oven glove and the spare key they had both spent years asking about.

“Well,” Martin said.

She handed it down.

Their father had tied green wool through the hole. Martin rubbed the knot with his thumb.

“We should leave it for whoever comes.”

“They’ll change the lock.”

From the chair, Ruth could see over the garden fence. Next door’s washing was out: two shirts, a towel, something small and blue.

“Give me your hand,” she said.

He put the key on the draining board and helped her down.

They worked until the boxes were full. At the door, Martin checked his pockets.

“Got everything?”

He nodded, then went back for the key.

Ruth waited while he tried it in the lock, although they both knew it would fit."
